A1.justification: Both complete, readable 34-page PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching the renumbered appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original VQA experiments, property-prediction evaluations and scaling analyses in Section 4 and Appendix E, including Tables 7–13.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and reports revised results in Section 4 and Appendix D, including Tables 7–13.

M1.justification: The representation extraction, T5 embeddings, representation conversion, transformer classifier and training objectives remain unchanged. DINOSAURv2 retains the same construction; its decoder-width adjustment is a model-size setting covered under E3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CLEVR6, CLEVRTex, Multi-dSprites and the same filtered VQA-v2 task. Property prediction, question categories and represented data domains are retained.

E2.justification: The same 15 upstream representation methods and question-only baseline are retained, with the same dataset-specific comparator exclusions. Removing a downstream depth configuration changes the experimental settings, not the comparator methods.

E3.justification: The systematic downstream depth grid changes from 2/5/15/20 layers to 2/5/15, with the stated model count falling from 852 to 640. Table 5 changes DINOSAURv2 training on CLEVR and Multi-dSprites from 500k to 250k steps and decoder hidden width from 512 to 1024. These are explicit setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish whether they reflect reruns or corrections. The separate T-20 comparison in Figure 8 remains.

E4.justification: Figures 3 and 14 lose the T-20 endpoint, removing the evidence and discussion of performance saturation beyond T-15 and Slot Attention's CLEVR deterioration. v3 additionally reports qualitative DINOSAURv2 hyperparameter sensitivity, without a quantified sweep. The other supplementary analysis questions remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-seed reporting for applicable models, one seed for foundation models, 95% confidence intervals and the same correlation-significance reporting practices. Revised numerical correlations and error bars do not introduce a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Revisions concentrate on DINOSAURv2 and derived analyses. Its reported T-15 accuracy changes from 87.0% to 94.3% on CLEVR and from 92.0% to 94.4% on Multi-dSprites-320k, now slightly exceeding DINOv2's unchanged 94.2% there (Tables 7 and 12). These accompany changed settings, not demonstrated same-setting gains. Figures 7/16 revise error reductions and identify CLIP rather than STEVE as the largest-gain case; question-category correlations also change. CLEVRTex and VQA-v2 table results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical specification of representations, downstream classification and property prediction is retained. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The claimed empirical scope narrows from over 800 models in the abstract and 852 in the introduction to over 600 and 640. The central contributions concerning foundation-model trade-offs, object-centric representations and their combination remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses DINOSAURv2's CLEVR shortfall and tentatively attributes it to hyperparameter sensitivity. It extends the representation-explicitness interpretation to Multi-dSprites and qualifies the property-prediction correlation as holding for most properties. The earlier explanation of Slot Attention's T-20 decline disappears.

D1.justification: Table 5 and Appendix A.1 revise DINOSAURv2's dataset-specific training and decoder settings. The previously stated VQA-v2 learning rate for T-20 is removed. A new reproducibility statement directs readers to implementation, dataset and metric details, without documenting a new code or data release.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work section retain the same works. Section 4.1 adds a limited positioning link by explicitly describing CNN/MultiCNN underperformance as consistent with Yoon et al. [32]; there is no broader novelty or literature revision.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the motivation, limitations and results discussion, plus terminology and typo corrections. The former Broader Impact appendix moves to an Ethics Statement, a Reproducibility Statement is added, and appendices B–E become A–D. The main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figures 3 and 14 change their axes and displayed depth configurations, Table 5 expands its dataset columns, and Figure 16 moves to the following page. Figure sizing, legends and surrounding layout receive limited adjustments. The same 27 figures and 13 tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves CLIP's error-reduction reporting: Figure 7 now shows roughly 49%, consistent with Tables 9 and 12, and adds useful sensitivity qualifications. However, it removes the scaling endpoint exposing Slot Attention's deterioration and leaves inconsistent DINOSAURv2 reporting: Table 7 gives 94.3% on CLEVR while unchanged Figure 11 retains scores around 87%. Tables 9–11 also revise overall scores without changing category scores. These benefits and unresolved empirical inconsistencies prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
